title: An idea worth building
cues: You have an idea. Your agent has a thousand defaults.
Before it builds another one, give it a direction.
Foreman starts with the person you are building for.
Find the references. Choose what belongs. Leave the rest.
Turn those decisions into a brief you can actually approve.
Then build. With the choices already made.
Check the details that turn a draft into a website.
Your idea. Built with intention. Meet Foreman.

title: Find your direction
cues: You know what you like. Until someone asks you why.
A hundred saved tabs will not answer that.
Give Foreman Board the brief. It looks for relevant references.
Look closer. The hierarchy. The spacing. The way it moves.
Keep the idea behind the design. Not somebody else's identity.
Bring those choices together into one direction.
Now your agent has something specific to build toward.
Less guessing. Start with Board.

title: Something feels wrong
cues: It works. So why does it still feel unfinished?
The answer is usually hiding in plain sight.
Ask Foreman Punch list to inspect the page.
A headline that says nothing. Three buttons competing for attention.
Text you can barely read. A layout that breaks on mobile.
Turn vague feedback into specific changes, in priority order.
Make the changes. Check the page again.
Keep what works. Fix what gets in the way.

title: Colour with a job to do
cues: A colour can look beautiful. And still fail on screen.
Start with a material. Ink, paper, polished metal.
Foreman Palette turns that reference into a working colour system.
Give every colour a job. Surface, text, action, feedback.
Check the contrast where people actually have to read.
Carry the same character from light into dark.
Save the tokens. Use them across the whole interface.
A palette you can build with.

title: Before the first click
cues: The website is finished. The launch is not.
Before the first click, check what people will find.
Foreman Launch walks through the domain and secure connection.
The preview that appears when someone shares your link.
The way back when a page goes missing.
The titles and sitemap that help search engines understand it.
Check what is ready. Keep track of what still needs you.
Then share it. With the details in place.
